title: Cloud Run and the VPC: private access to a database

videos.script: A Cloud Run service deploys, answers its health check, and hangs on its first query. This lesson is about why, and what fixes it. {{why}} An instance runs on Google's network, not on yours. Your database has a private address, and there is no route to it. {{direct}} The first fix is direct VPC egress. Each instance takes an address in a subnet of your network. Nothing extra runs, and nothing extra is billed. What you plan is the subnet, because a full subnet stops new instances. {{connector}} The older fix is a connector. It is a few small machines in your network that forward the traffic. They are billed all month, even at night. {{both}} You will also see a check that Terraform makes, and one it cannot make. {{settings}} Last, two settings people mix up. Ingress decides who may call the service. Egress decides where its own connections go. Changing one never changes the other.
